liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Doll** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls China Doll nice, and finds the Help>Slip>Franklin's sequence interesting; Reviewer feels the band, especially Jerry, falters in China Doll [34][35][36]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer says Minglewood is really hot and deserves recognition; The recording cuts abruptly at the very beginning of Minglewood Blues [17][36]
- **Slipknot!** (2 reviews): Reviewer praises Jerry's playing in an inspired Slipknot, with turns predating his MIDI guitar sounds; Reviewer says Slipknot is jam-packed and Help starts with a mellow opening [31][35]
- **Wharf Rat** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls Wharf Rat one for the ages; Reviewer was blown away by Wharf Rat emerging out of Space [31][34]
- **Help On The Way** (1 review): Reviewer says the opening of Help is disorganized, with the band not tightly together at the start [26]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Reviewer calls Franklin's Tower on fire, and the Slipknot a bit short but nice [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-04-21.u87.eaton-silberman.10035.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 23 songs; 180 min; rated 4.6/5 by 10 [1]
- **gd1984-04-21.137271.mtx.tobin.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 170 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1984-04-21.148829.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.bryant.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 24 songs; 170 min [8]
- **gd84-04-21.neumann.nawrocki.18253.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 22 songs; 181 min; rated 4.04/5 by 26 [14]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the instrument separation in the recording excellent; Reviewer says it puts you in the Civic Center, regularly cited among the best audience recordings; Reviewer says the audience recording is echoey with strong bass, balanced except Jerry's guitar, which sits low [28][33][37]
- **gd1984-04-21.neumannu87.bandrofcheck.34682.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 22 songs; 184 min; rated 2/5 by 1 [15]
- **gd1984-04-21.166581.mtx.seamons.ht166.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 170 min [17]. Said about its sound: Lamarre's recording supplies deep bass for the soundboard mixes; treble on these Philly shows was EQ'd per source [17]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended this as their first concert [30]
- Reviewer notes Jerry's voice is gruff, typical for 1984 [32]
- Taper was very sick that night and started set two on the wrong tape side, requiring a patch [15]
- Reviewer says this show is overshadowed by the previous night's April 20 show, yet is the one they have played most [26]
- Reviewer ranks the pre-drums segment among the best of 1984 [31]
- Reviewer attended this and Providence on 26 April, judging Providence the best show of the tour [36]
- Reviewer finds the show clean and lacking the sloppiness of some other 1984 shows [37]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-04-21.u87.eaton-silberman.10035.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Rob Eaton and Jeff Silberman; transferred by Doug Oade; source: Rob's Neumann u87 (cardiod setting, split 30', 17th row) > 6 x 9 volts > Teac mic transformers -> Jeff's Technics SV-100 line in @ 14 bits > DAT [1]
- **gd1984-04-21.137271.mtx.tobin.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: Matrix 2 Source Mix - SBD (shnid=137247) Recording Info: SBD > Cassette Master > Reel > Dat (Panasonic SV-3800/48k); Transfer Info: Dat (Sony R500) > Tascam… [2]
- **gd1984-04-21.148829.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.bryant.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Robert Bryant; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Robert Bryant's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Schoeps CMC4 MK41 mics > Sony D5 [8]. Also: Patches from the Neumann U87 source fill 27 seconds in China Doll to Don't Need Love and 10 seconds in Drums [8]
- **gd84-04-21.neumann.nawrocki.18253.sbeok.shnf**: Reviewer says the microphones were spread 30 feet apart in row 17, feeding an early-generation digital deck [33]
- **gd1984-04-21.neumannu87.bandrofcheck.34682.sbeok.shnf**: source: unknown shotgun mics > Sony D6 > Maxell MX 90s (MC) > Marantz PRD505 (azimuth adjusted) > Marantz Intergrated Stereo Amp MP-68 > SBLive! > SoundForge 5.0… [15]. Also: Taper used Neumann U87s through a Sony mixer and Technics PCM into DAT, then CDR; The end of Throwing Stones, Not Fade Away and Brokedown Palace come from the LMA copy [15]
- **gd1984-04-21.166581.mtx.seamons.ht166.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut w/EQ > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) December 26, 2023 [17]. Also: Matrix by Seamons uses Eaton and Silberman's Neumann U87 DAT to patch gaps between songs in the audience track [17]

claims.text: Reviewer says this show is overshadowed by the previous night's April 20 show, yet is the one they have played most
Reviewer says the opening of Help is disorganized, with the band not tightly together at the start
Reviewer calls Franklin's Tower on fire, and the Slipknot a bit short but nice
Reviewer finds the instrument separation in the recording excellent
Reviewer attended this as their first concert
Reviewer praises Jerry's playing in an inspired Slipknot, with turns predating his MIDI guitar sounds
Reviewer calls Wharf Rat one for the ages
Reviewer ranks the pre-drums segment among the best of 1984
Reviewer notes Jerry's voice is gruff, typical for 1984
Reviewer says the microphones were spread 30 feet apart in row 17, feeding an early-generation digital deck
Reviewer says it puts you in the Civic Center, regularly cited among the best audience recordings
Reviewer was blown away by Wharf Rat emerging out of Space
Reviewer calls China Doll nice, and finds the Help>Slip>Franklin's sequence interesting
Reviewer says Slipknot is jam-packed and Help starts with a mellow opening
Reviewer feels the band, especially Jerry, falters in China Doll
Reviewer says Minglewood is really hot and deserves recognition
Reviewer says the band fumbled the return to lyrics after the jam
Reviewer attended this and Providence on 26 April, judging Providence the best show of the tour
Reviewer says the audience recording is echoey with strong bass, balanced except Jerry's guitar, which sits low
Reviewer finds the show clean and lacking the sloppiness of some other 1984 shows
This is a matrix recording by Tobin
Master is a Robert Bryant FOB cassette source, transferred by Charlie Miller, using Schoeps mics
Patches from the Neumann U87 source fill 27 seconds in China Doll to Don't Need Love and 10 seconds in Drums
Taper used Neumann U87s through a Sony mixer and Technics PCM into DAT, then CDR
Taper was very sick that night and started set two on the wrong tape side, requiring a patch
The end of Throwing Stones, Not Fade Away and Brokedown Palace come from the LMA copy
Matrix by Seamons uses Eaton and Silberman's Neumann U87 DAT to patch gaps between songs in the audience track
Lamarre's recording supplies deep bass for the soundboard mixes; treble on these Philly shows was EQ'd per source
The recording cuts abruptly at the very beginning of Minglewood Blues
